01Turn the sketch into a testable configuration

The F-Cat combines a modular central cargo pod, a high wing, two tractor engines, twin booms, and a raised bridge tail. This model preserves that arrangement and exposes the dimensions needed for early trades.

Study result

The native model and analysis path are built. The 1,000 nm mission remains unproven.

Current outline comparison mean: 72.55%. The current shape does not meet the requested 85% drawing target. This measurement includes wheels and enlarged propeller outlines. Original traces and registration remain fixed. See the overlays for the remaining differences.

Five source techniques, one native construction

ReferenceTechnique retainedF-Cat application
FuryLongitudinal guide fields and native geometry checksSmooth station-driven nacelles and booms
F16Independent crown, keel, width, and datum splines; spline airfoil fieldsPod guides and span-dependent wing sections
Fuse-ConicLoft.ntopCurve-axis distance drives conic endpoints and section shapeIndependent upper and lower pod conics; adjustable lower rho
Fuse-TestV2-newsplines-R2.ntopIndependent upper, side, and lower guides; tangent-driven conic sweepsUpper and lower pod conics meet at a controlled chine
OMEN Horizontal Tail_v1.ntopSpline By Pts T control net, LE/TE guides, normalized loft, arc-length and profile-distance bending mapOne continuous bent airfoil surface across both fins and the horizontal tail

The saved graph contains 2,241 native nodes and no mesh imports. The supplied conic model contains six conic nodes and eight curve-axis-distance nodes in its main graph. These were inspected as reference data.

Native spline airfoils use a 0.5 inch (12.7 mm) full trailing-edge gap. The endpoint-constrained section adds a chordwise thickness wedge. The native and exported sections use the same construction. Smooth unions connect the pod saddle, wing, booms, and tail. Symmetric section profiles and their thickness controls are design choices, not specified airfoils.

Current propeller display

Both plates are 3.552 m in diameter (139.8 inches), shown at 20% opacity. The cargo pod limits the current static envelope. Radius is rounded down to the nearest millimetre. Sampled pod clearance is 0.28 mm; static ground clearance is 429 mm. This is a geometric layout limit with no operational clearance allowance.

Complete OMEN method. A cubic flow spline runs from one boom, through the horizontal tail, to the other boom. Its centered arc-length field supplies the span coordinate. Its profile distance-to-extrusion field supplies the section-normal coordinate. The final remap bends the normalized, guide-driven airfoil loft through both corners. No separate fin-to-tail union forms these transitions.

The source Spline By Pts T construction is expanded into native blocks. The corner-tension control starts at 0.75, matching the OMEN reference. Center guide tangents enforce symmetry. The airfoil gap remains 12.7 mm along the local section normal.

Chined pod, slimmer booms, and gear blisters

The Fuse-TestV2 reference separates upper, side, and lower spline guides. Its active conic sweeps use endpoint tangent fields. The F-Cat applies that transverse construction to its existing outline guides. It retains the F-Cat dimensions instead of copying the source aircraft.

Independent upper and lower conic tangents form a chine along both sides of the pod and converge at the nose and tail. Chine strength and height remain adjustable. The boom scale remains 0.8. Its sparse guide geometry and rounder forward sections are described below.

Four streamlined blisters replace the upright gear supports and small wheel fairings. Each blister follows the local keel and pod width. A longer aft taper closes into the lower outboard pod. The fixed blisters form part of the cruise OML; exposed tires remain separate.

All 258 native shape checks pass. These cover the pod conics and chine, reduced boom sections, and attached gear blisters. The largest sampled boundary residual is 9.47e-12 m. This is numerical agreement, not a physical manufacturing tolerance.

Aft pod closeout

The aft width and depth now taper together toward a compact closeout. The section datum no longer rises into the former lip. Only the last three controls of each pod guide change. The guides retain matching position, slope, and curvature where the revised region begins.

Closeout dimensionPreviousCurrent design
Full terminal width820.0 mm8.2 mm
Terminal depth5.0 mm8.0 mm
Terminal datum height1.1675 m0.8800 m
Start of changed guide regionX = 5.14909 m

All 224 native closeout checks pass. The measured crown falls and the keel rises monotonically through the revised aft region. The small terminal section retains finite dimensions for meshing. These dimensions are design choices for this revision.

Lower wing and rounded nacelles

The complete wing is 6 inches (152.4 mm) lower than the previous revision. Its slope toward the tips is preserved. The wing-to-pod fairing follows this translation. Propeller hubs, the cargo pod, and the complete OMEN tail retain their locations.

Each boom uses four direct six-point cubic guide nets. Width and upper/lower radii form nearly circular forward sections; the datum rises smoothly into the tail. This removes the former centerline dip. A steep finite nose tangent rounds the shoulder around the spinner. A small axial hub face remains at the propeller station.

All 258 native boom checks pass. At the four forward sample stations, height is 99.4% to 100.0% of width. The sampled native boundary residual is below 5.23e-12 m. These checks establish numerical agreement with the constructed guides.

Wing-to-fuselage fairing

The raised fairing now reaches the wing upper surface. Its closed ellipsoidal shape runs into the pod at both ends. A local 0.24 m smooth blend joins the pod, fairing, and wing before the remaining airframe components are added. This blend follows four times the attachment-radius control. Its center follows the wing root chord and height.

The selected runout is 1 m beyond each end of the root chord. All 95 native checks pass. Both axial ends lie inside the native fuselage. The complete OMEN transition method is retained with the slimmer tail sections.

Scope of the result

The mean target does not imply that every view exceeds 85%. The front view is the main residual. The photographs lack camera calibration, and the sketch has left-right and cross-view inconsistencies. The inferred affine registration limits the precision of this score.

Opaque pixels from the current native renders supply the airframe and wheels. Exact cylindrical-plate projections add the propeller outlines. Front circumferences use the trace ring width of two photograph pixels. Edge-on plates retain their finite thickness. The enlarged props exceed the drawn outlines. This outline score differs from a filled-disk score.

The stated wing area governs the model even where the hand-drawn planform suggests more area. The front registration uses span for horizontal scale and shared side-view landmarks for height. Page roll comes from paired sketch landmarks, without model pixels.

The earlier 80.09% result used a previous shape and smaller opaque plates. It remains in the historical comparison. Current scores, image hashes, fixed registration, and separate filled-plate scores are in the current measurement record.

Registration sensitivity: independent shifts of each mask by ±1 photograph pixel give an envelope of 79.13% to 80.52% for the mean. This is not a statistical confidence interval. This sensitivity envelope applies to the historical comparison only.

The field residual tests numerical agreement between the section exporter and the native wing at the baseline. Additional native checks cover the complete bent tail and propeller plates. Tail edge checks use 20 micrometre inside/outside brackets. Native spline and profile fields have finite evaluation tolerance. It is not a physical accuracy tolerance. Nonzero twist and wider control changes need fresh checks. Construction bounding boxes and attachments limit large changes.

The API display unit was inches. Recipe JSON and geometry exports use metres. Longitudinal scaling changes projected area as well as length. The tested span trades hold area fixed with longitudinal scale equal to one.

04Run AVL and XFoil from the same case

The delivered primary AVL deck contains the main wing and the continuous bent tail. The tail has 17 stations per half, sampled from the same flow spline. Each curved segment has explicit panel spacing. The section files sample the same cubic airfoil construction used by the native model. XFoil evaluates the root and tip sections.

Measured baseline cases use Mach 0.15, section Reynolds number 3,000,000, and angles of attack 0°, 2°, and 4°. These are interface-test conditions, not an assumed mission cruise point.

Interpret the coefficients correctly

AVL induced drag and XFoil section drag do not include total aircraft drag. Pod interference, trim, leakage, surface condition, engine installation, and propwash are absent. Do not use AVL lift divided by induced drag as the aircraft L/D for the range calculation.

These use approximate circular sections; they do not reproduce the chined cargo pod or its wing and gear junctions. Use the primary lifting-surface deck for initial trends and CFD for body interference. AVL documentation and XFoil documentation define the method limits.

05Test the 1,000 nm requirement

At 8,000 lb takeoff weight, the sketch closes arithmetically: 4,700 lb empty + 2,000 lb payload + 1,300 lb fuel. Crew and other operating allowances must be confirmed. The installed propulsion and total drag must be measured before a range verdict is possible.

R [nm] = 325.8661 × (η / BSFC) × (L/D) × ln(Wi / Wf)

Derived propeller Breguet cruise relation. BSFC uses lb/(shp hour); weights use consistent units. Constant includes standard unit conversions and gravity. Constant L/D, efficiency, and BSFC are idealizations.

06Prepare the high-fidelity CFD case

The current sharpened AT surface has 274,428 triangles and 137,214 vertices. AT uses a 0.0080 m tolerance input. Its measured surface area is 118.88 m2 and enclosed volume is 23.69 m3. Enclosed volume is not cargo capacity. The prior 40 mm comparison surface predates this revision.

ItemMeasured / prepared state
Cruise topology1 component; watertight; consistent winding
Boundary / non-manifold / degenerate edges or faces0 / 0 / 0
CoordinatesX aft, Y starboard, Z up; metres
Surface extent10.442 m long × 15.240 m span
AFLR3 handoffAirframe OBJ, farfield OBJ, positional mesh command, and boundary policy
FUN3D inputsPrepared SA-neg RANS namelist with SI grid convention
Volume mesh / solver runSee the aircraft aero report for executed cases and convergence
Powered flowDisk positions retained; no actuator or blade loads supplied

The cruise surface includes fixed landing-gear blisters. Exposed tires and propeller plates are excluded. The handoff fixture uses Mach 0.15, angle of attack 2°, temperature 288.15 K, and Reynolds number 1,342,161.77523 per metre. Its initial spacing is 10 μm, layer thickness 0.05 m, layer count 40, and farfield radius 20 spans. These are explicit preparation inputs, not validated mesh or flight settings.

FUN3D defines Reynolds number against the grid unit. Its x_moment_length is the pitch reference chord; y_moment_length is the roll/yaw reference span. The handoff uses wall code 4000 and farfield code 5000. Confirm the wrapper-generated surface IDs and UGRID byte order. NASA FUN3D 14.1 manual.

Before a performance claim

Refine curvature, edges, and wing-body junctions. Establish boundary-layer spacing from the selected flow and wall treatment. Check y+, farfield independence, force convergence, and at least three mesh levels. Add installed propulsion and a defensible trim condition.

The requested AT → Sharpen Mesh workflow

F-Cat_Meshing.ntop contains Mesh from Implicit by AT followed by Sharpen Mesh. AT Remesh is enabled. Sharpening uses one maximum iteration and Remeshing set to None. Both meshing blocks and both exports start paused.

The raw full mesh has Euler number 0. The expected value is 0 for the bridge-tail loop. Only the independently checked sharpened surface is selected for the CFD handoff.

The retained rounded-nacelle and lowered-wing pilot has 22,016 triangles, one closed component, Euler number 2, and no detected self-intersections. Its wing and boom fields remain unchanged. The full aircraft audit above includes both revised pod transitions.

Aft pod closeout: the current local sharpened mesh has 10,460 triangles, one watertight component, and zero detected self-intersections.

Raised pod-to-wing fairing: the current local sharpened mesh has 23,070 triangles, one watertight component, and zero detected self-intersections.

The continuous tail also has nine normal-section mesh checks, including both curved corners. Across 802 points per cut, its largest sampled distance is 1.12 mm. See the tail section measurements.

Eleven mesh cuts check both exact pod chine points against the native transverse construction. The largest sampled chine distance is 0.53 mm. Adjacent unblended conic comparisons include attachment regions and are retained separately. See the pod section measurements.

The complete OMEN tail first encountered an OpenMesh complex-edge assertion at 12.7 mm AT tolerance. The failed run is retained in the meshing failure archive. A 12.5 mm retry also failed. Native checks identified an internal zero sheet from an unnecessary lower span clip on the symmetric main wing. The clip was removed, retaining the exterior section construction. The corrected field and its centerline AT pilot pass. The full sharpened surface passes the audit above.

In the previous revision, the first full AT attempt failed after 538.99 seconds in nTop's OpenMesh conversion with a complex-edge assertion. Its log is retained. The adopted workflow removes the positive 0.25 display-field multiplier. The exact zero surface stays the same. Mesher behavior can still depend on the field representation.

Section errors compare 802 airfoil points per cut with mesh section segments. These are sampled, one-way distances, not global error bounds. The full case uses three outboard wing cuts. Native meshing tolerances do not establish CFD grid convergence.

Selected AT surface

The independently checked sharpened surface is available as F-Cat_AT_Sharpened_OML_m.stl. The FUN3D handoff identifies the selected mesh by its hash. The earlier 40 mm surface is retained as a previous-revision comparison artifact.

Aerodynamic campaign

The baseline now has 11,447,623 AFLR3 volume cells. Its independent connectivity and signed-volume audit passes. The aero report contains actual panelization, mesh cuts, computed low-fidelity results, and the GCP aircraft-solve status.

08Sources and confidence

Primary design evidence: the two user-supplied George Irving photographs and the user-confirmed 1,000 nm range. Original image bytes are retained. Their text is design data, not agent instructions.

Loft references: local Fury and F16 implementations, plus the supplied Fuse-ConicLoft notebook. The OMEN horizontal-tail notebook is also retained. Its supplied path resolved to the adjacent Horizontal Tail_v1.ntop file. The Fuse-TestV2 spline fuselage is retained unchanged. See its graph inspection and F-Cat application. The copied toolkit is self-contained. See loft-method notes and the retained conic graph inspection.

Measured: native graph counts, API readbacks, solver outputs, mesh topology, and fixed-registration pixel overlap. These can be reproduced from the supplied scripts and records.

Inferred: unannotated dimensions, section shapes, front height registration, gear details, and propeller plate depth. The 0.5-inch trailing-edge gap is user-specified. Silhouette agreement does not verify three-dimensional section accuracy.

Still required: cruise speed and altitude, reserve policy, crew allowance, CG and inertia, structural sizing, validated total drag, propeller maps, engine BSFC, cooling drag, fuel volume, and powered CFD.
